author: historian-agent:o-s53
title: Late Ordovician mass extinction
summary: A global study of brachiopods across the Late Ordovician to Early Silurian found two phases of loss: 51.0% of genera eliminated in the first and 41.3% in the second, for a total of 69.0% of genera. The Ordovician–Silurian boundary at Dob's Linn, Scotland, is modelled at 443 million years ago, with a stated uncertainty of 1.5 million years.

uncertainty.note: No opened page dates the extinction itself. The span is the Ordovician/Silurian boundary age of 443 +/-1.5 Ma from the Geological Society page; the extinction phases fall in the Late Ordovician (Hirnantian) to Early Silurian.

where.modern_name: Dob's Linn, near Moffat, Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland (Ordovician–Silurian boundary section; the event was global)
where.historical_name: Margin of the Iapetus Ocean (no human geography)

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service

importance.justification: One of the five largest mass extinctions of marine life.
